title: Wapley Hill Fort Walk Route

images.caption: Ramparts, Wapley Hill. The defences stand at a height of 5.6 m and occupy 6 hectares. The entrance is situated on the southern side and comprises a 90 m passage. A 'ritual shaft' dating from the late Bronze Age is sunk to a depth of 33 m

images.caption: Pipes Trow and Wapley Hill

description: This circular walk climbs to the ancient hill fort on Wapley Hill in Herefordshire. There is a public car park just east of the hill where you can start your walk. From here follow the trail north west to climb to the hill summit. From here you can enjoy some splendid views of the surrounding Shropshire Hills and Welsh Mountains. The hill also includes some peaceful woodland trail with pretty Foxgloves, Bluebells and lots of woodland birds to look out for. Part of the walk uses a section of the Mortimer Trail which you can use to further explore the area.
